title: The whole model ships as one JSON file of explicit trees
context: train_synth.py writes weights/tpms.json: every tree node as JSON arrays rounded to 4 decimals, plus encoding, seeds and eval. 20-predictor.js fetches it, 11-forest.js repacks it into 12-byte binary node records, then drops the parsed JSON. The file is now 38 MB (36.6 MB per docs/HOW-TO-retrain-synth.md); README still says 15 MB.

options.name: One JSON bundle (current)
options.summary: Human-readable, single fetch, gzip on the wire from GitHub Pages.
pros: Simple to inspect and diff the meta block
cons: Over GitHub's 25 MB browser upload, so deploys go through GitHub Desktop or a zip handed to Claude
Parse cost and memory spike before packing
Each retrain adds ~38 MB to git history

options.name: JSON meta plus a binary tree file
options.summary: Trainer emits the same 12-byte packed records Synth already builds, as a .bin beside a small JSON.
pros: Roughly a third of the size, no parse step
Browser can use the buffer directly
cons: Trainer must replicate the packing (already specified in 11-forest.js)

options.name: Shrink the JSON
options.summary: Fewer trees, 3 decimals, or split per metric.
cons: Costs R² or only delays the problem as Vault grows

recommendation: train_synth.py _serialize_tree, 20-predictor.js loadFamily and 11-forest.js pack show the JSON-then-pack path; README "Versioning" ties the bundle's meta block to cache busting.
strain: The bundle grew from 15 MB to 36.6 MB and no longer uploads through GitHub's web UI; NEXT-UP lists serving it gzipped or split as an idea.

log_refs.entry: Ideas: Serve the model gzipped or split it
